seattle-seahawks:control:2026-07-11:100.text: Paul Allen's will required the estate to sell the team and route the proceeds to philanthropy, so the estate launched the sale on February 18, 2026, ten days after the Super Bowl LX win.

Allen & Co. ran a five-month process that drew at least six suitors and four formal bids, and it came down to Khosla against a Wyc Grousbeck and Aditya Mittal group. That head-to-head finish pushed the price to $9.612B, 59% above the Commanders' $6.05B record.
NFL control stakes almost never trade, and this one hit the market as the reigning champion. Khosla said it plainly: 'How often do you get to buy a franchise that just won the Super Bowl?'

The price works out to roughly 13.6x to 15.0x revenue, the highest multiple ever paid for a team. It beat the 13.4x that Arctos paid for its Browns stake two months earlier and reflects rising national media money and strong demand for live sports.

minnesota-timberwolves:control:2026-08-2.text: Marc Stad was already a minority owner of the Wolves and Lynx, and he runs Dragoneer, a growth investor managing about $35B. An insider who knows the books and has deep capital behind him can pay a 12.5% premium to Forbes with confidence.
The $4.5B price triples the $1.5B that Lore and Rodriguez agreed to pay in 2021. It lands in a market reset by the Celtics at $6.1B and the Lakers at $10B and then $12.5B.
The NBA's 11-year, $76B national deal with Disney, NBC and Amazon began in 2025-26. It pays about $6.9B a season, 160% more than the old contract.
Target Center is the NBA's second-oldest arena, and ownership is already working with Minneapolis on a new building. A new arena is revenue upside that the current Forbes number does not capture.

los-angeles-lakers:control:2026-08-12:na.text: Josh Kushner (Thrive Capital) and former Disney CEO Bob Iger were pursuing a Las Vegas expansion team before they pivoted to the Lakers. Iger says the deal came together in three days. Trophy buyers with an expansion fee as their fallback paid $12.5B, 25% over Forbes.
The price resets the top of the market at $2.5B above the Lakers' own 2025 record. It also clears the Seahawks' $9.6B and roughly doubles the Celtics' $6.1B.

A control buyer can amortize 100% of the franchise's tax basis over 15 years under Sec. 197. The final One Big Beautiful Bill Act dropped the House proposal to cap that at 50%, so the full write-off on a $12.5B basis remains available.

los-angeles-lakers:control:2025-06-18:na.text: Mark Walter already owned 26% of the Lakers, bought from Phil Anschutz in 2021, along with a right of first refusal on the majority stake. He also controls the Dodgers and the Sparks, so he was the natural buyer.
This was the first change of control in 46 years of Buss family ownership. The family keeps an interest, and Jeanie Buss stays governor for at least five years after closing.
The deal was signed weeks before the NBA's $76B, 11-year national package kicked in for 2025-26. That package pays about $6.9B a season, 160% more than the old deal.
At $10B, the Lakers priced 64% above the Celtics' $6.1B sale three months earlier and nearly 3x the Mavericks' $3.5B in 2023. That is how fast the top of the NBA market was rerating.

boston-celtics:control:2025-03-20:51.text: The Grousbeck family put the team up for sale for estate planning reasons. As NBA franchises appreciate, they become harder to pass down under estate tax and league ownership rules.

Existing co-owner Steve Pagliuca lost with what he called a fully guaranteed and financed offer at a record price. Chisholm had to top a real competing bid to get to $6.1B, just above the Commanders' $6.05B record.
Buyers were underwriting the NBA's new $76B, 11-year national deal starting in 2025-26. It pays about $6.9B a season, 160% more than the expiring contract.

portland-trail-blazers:control:2025-09-1.text: Paul Allen's will required his teams to be sold with the proceeds going to philanthropy. The estate was a motivated seller, and the first tranche priced only 11% above Forbes in a hot NBA market.
Oregon passed SB 1501 to borrow $365M for Moda Center renovations, repaid over two decades from tax revenue. That keeps the franchise in Portland and puts public money behind the building.
Dundon bought at the start of the NBA's $76B, 11-year national deal, which pays about $6.9B a season from 2025-26, 160% more than before.
The Allen estate, bound by Paul Allen's will to sell and give the proceeds to philanthropy, agreed up front to sell the last 19.9% to the Dundon group. That tranche closes by 2028.
The deferred 19.9% is priced at $4.5B, $500M above the first 80.1%. It sits on a franchise that Oregon's $365M Moda Center renovation bill now anchors in Portland.

atlanta-falcons:minority:2026-08-20:10.text: The Falcons earned an estimated $800M in 2024 revenue, 8th in the NFL, with more than $100M a year from sponsorship. Mercedes-Benz Stadium ranks first among NFL venues in non-football event gross revenue, and the Forbes team number does not fully capture that.
This is Arctos' fourth NFL stake, after the Bills, Chargers and Browns. A repeat buyer with league approval and deal data from three other clubs can underwrite a $10.6B blended valuation.
NFL rules cap approved funds at 10% of a team, which makes LP slots scarce. Several teams have now sold limited stakes above $10B even though no NFL control sale has topped $10B.
The Falcons were valued at $8B in September 2025. Eleven months later Arctos priced them at $10.6B, with the second tranche stepping up to about $11B in 18 months.

cleveland-browns:minority:2026-05-19:3.text: Arctos money helps fund the Browns' new $2.6B stadium in Brook Park, with Jimmy and Dee Haslam pledging $1.76B. A new stadium is upside that the Forbes team value does not reflect.
This was Arctos' third NFL stake and its first deal after KKR bought the firm. Arctos manages about $16B and holds stakes in 32 teams, so it brings comps and conviction a one-off buyer lacks.

NFL rules allow passive PE stakes of 3% to 10% per team, with a six-team cap and a six-year minimum hold, and Arctos is the only firm approved across multiple NFL teams. That scarcity of approved capital lets the Haslams sell in tranches at a premium.
The $9B valuation equals roughly 13.4x revenue, the highest multiple on record until the Seahawks sale two months later.

las-vegas-raiders:minority:2026-05-14:25.text: The buyers step into a pre-cleared succession: Egon Durban holds a right of first refusal on control when Mark Davis, who has no heir, sells. A minority block with a defined path to control is worth more than a passive LP slice.

The buyer group is Silver Lake co-CEO Durban (taking him to 22%), Michael Dell, Blackstone's Joseph Baratta and TKO executives. First Football paid a weighted valuation of about $700M in 2007 and exits at $9.9B.

las-vegas-raiders:minority:2026-03-31:3..text: The deal gave Egon Durban a 10-year right of first refusal on Mark Davis's controlling stake, making him Davis's successor. The $11.1B headline also includes the 10% flip tax paid to the league, so it overstates the value of a pure LP stake.
The 2020 move to Las Vegas, Allegiant Stadium and rising NFL media and venue revenue pushed the valuation to $11.1B, up from earlier estimates of $7.8B.

miami-dolphins:minority:2026-03-03:1.text: The 1% is in Stephen Ross's holding company, which owns the Dolphins plus Hard Rock Stadium, the F1 Miami Grand Prix and the Miami Open. The $12.5B covers a stadium-and-events platform, not just a football team.
Ares bought 10% at an $8.1B valuation in December 2024, and Joseph Tsai and Oliver Weisberg bought 3% at the same mark. Fifteen months later the holding company priced 54% higher.
Ross bought the team for $1B in 2009, has no plans to sell, and reportedly turned down offers near $15B. With control off the table, a 1% slice is the only way in, and small slices price richly.
Xiaomi co-founder Lin Bin called the stake a financial opportunity and 'a wonderful investment and learning opportunity.' He is a trophy buyer writing a small check into a record valuation.

new-england-patriots:minority:2025-09-25.text: Kraft keeps full control and the proceeds stay in the franchise to be reinvested, so the $9B is a pre-money mark on a passive stake with no path to control. That caps the premium at 12.5% over Forbes.
Sixth Street already owns pieces of the Celtics, Spurs and San Francisco Giants. Dean Metropoulos is a consumer-brand investor who bought and sold Pabst and Hostess.

san-francisco-49ers:minority:2025-09-24:.text: Briger bought at the same valuation as the May 2025 sale, about $8.6B, for roughly $275M. The Yorks keep about 87.8%, so this is a passive slice priced off a fresh comp, not a new negotiation.
Pete Briger is executive chairman of Fortress Investment Group, which oversees more than $53B. He is a Menlo Park local who framed the purchase around the Bay Area rather than returns.

san-francisco-49ers:minority:2025-05-16:.text: The $8.6B mark broke the NFL minority-stake record of $8.3B set by the Eagles a year earlier. The buyers paid $533.2M for 6.2%.
The York family still owns 91%, and minority shares carry a discount because they come with no control. That is why the price trails where a control sale would land.
The buyers were three Bay Area families, Khosla, Deeter and Griffith, rooted in tech and venture capital. They were local, wealthy LPs, not return-driven funds.

new-york-giants:minority:2025-09-03:10.text: This was the first outside investment in a franchise the Mara family has controlled since 1925. A 10% block of a century-old New York franchise had never been available.
The Mara and Tisch families hired Moelis & Co. in February 2025 to run the minority sale. The banked process produced a $10B-plus valuation that topped the Commanders' $6.05B control record.

Julia Koch has a net worth of about $81.2B, and her family bought 15% of BSE Global, owner of the Nets and Liberty, the year before. For that buyer, a $1B-plus check for a trophy New York asset is routine.

chicago-bears:minority:2025-08-07:2.35.text: The 2.35% came from the estate of the late Andrew McKenna and was bought by the existing owners. After the deal, the McCaskeys hold 77% and the Ryans 23%.
The $8.9B valuation includes the Bears' 326-acre Arlington Heights property, where the team planned a new stadium. That land and stadium upside sits outside a team-only Forbes number.

los-angeles-chargers:minority:2025-05-15.text: This was Arctos' second NFL stake, after it bought 10% of the Bills in January 2025. The firm was building a multi-team NFL book under the new PE rules.

Arctos took a passive 8% while the Spanos family keeps about 61%. It followed Tom and Holly Gores' 27% purchase, which carried no control or path to control, so the price was set for a non-control stake.

dallas-mavericks:control:2023-12-27:69.text: The Adelson family, which controls Las Vegas Sands, wants an integrated casino resort in Dallas, and Cuban had floated a new arena inside such a development. The $3.5B beat Sportico's $2.77B December mark on that development vision.
Miriam Adelson funded the deal partly by selling $2B of Sands stock. Cuban put the fit plainly: 'They're not basketball people. I'm not real estate people.'

washington-commanders:control:2023-05-12.text: Dan Snyder sold under heavy pressure from workplace misconduct and financial investigations, which ended in a $60M NFL fine. Owners wanted him out.

Josh Harris and Steve Apostolopoulos both submitted formal bids. Harris raised his offer to $6.05B to win what Apostolopoulos called a 'head to head' process, and the price beat the Broncos' $4.65B record.
Harris co-founded Apollo and already owned the 76ers and Devils. He assembled a 20-LP group within the NFL's 25-partner limit and met the league's $1.1B debt cap.

minnesota-timberwolves:control:2021-04-1.text: Glen Taylor tried to terminate the sale in March 2024, but an arbitration panel ordered it to proceed. He had to finish at the $1.5B price fixed in April 2021.
By closing in June 2025, NBA revenue had soared and the team was valued at $3.1B (Forbes) to $3.29B (Sportico). The $1.5B is a stale 2021 price, not a market comp.
